title: Cohort Perturbation Explorer: quantization slice stability (int4/awq/gptq)
content:
Objective:
Describe slice-level quality deltas observed when moving baseline fp16 -> int8 -> int4 (AWQ, GPTQ) for the latest onboarding candidate (model X v1.3). Provide per-cohort breakdown, human spotcheck notes, and short-term mitigations for production rollout decisions. This doc is an experimental/runbook-style notebook, not final sign-off.

Executive summary (short):
- Overall token-level loss increase is small for int8 (~+0.6% avg) but grows for int4 variants: AWQ-int4 shows a median metric delta of -2.8% on our acceptability metric, GPTQ-int4 shows -3.9% (worse on specific cohorts).
- Quality regressions concentrate in predictable cohorts: math/precision, multi-turn context retention (long-context), and rare-domain factuals. Conversational safety and style are largely preserved.
- Human spotchecks show AWQ-int4 tends to hallucinate numeric paraphrases (rounded/extrapolated values) more aggressively than GPTQ-int4, while GPTQ-int4 shows brittle tokenization-driven truncation in code examples.
- Recommended immediate action: block default int4 for the model in hosted tier until per-route routing is enabled; enable int8 as balanced fallback and roll out selective int4 on low-risk read-only endpoints (embeds, summarization) with monitoring.

Dataset and prompt sets used:
- Core prompt bank: 7k prompts used for onboarding (mix of open-source benchmarks + internal promptset). Split into: calibration (1k), heldout evaluation (5k), human-spotcheck pool (1k).
- Slices (cohorts) curated by applied-ml: long-context-instruction (500 prompts), code-gen-snippets (420), arithmetic-exact (320), multi-step-reasoning (410), domain-legal-terms (240), non_english-fr (300), repetition-hallucination (200), short-answer-facts (600).
- Prompts include prefix variability, truncated context scenarios, and adversarial perturbations (token deletions / paraphrase swaps) used to surface brittleness.

Evaluation methodology (brief):
- Models: baseline fp16 (server-ff16), int8 (symmetric quant profile), AWQ-int4 (release candidate tuning), GPTQ-int4 (calibrated with per-channel knobs).
- Metrics: acceptability (automated classifier + human-aligned score), exact-match where applicable (math/code), RLHF-style preference rate (pairwise head-to-head on 1k comparisons), perplexity drift, and token error patterns (OOV insert/drop).
- Statistical checks: bootstrap CI on deltas, Bonferroni correction when scanning multiple slices, and stratified human spotchecks focused on top-3 regressed slices.

Key numerical findings (high level):
- Global acceptability delta vs fp16: int8: -0.6% (CI [-0.9,-0.3]), AWQ-int4: -2.8% (CI [-3.4,-2.2]), GPTQ-int4: -3.9% (CI [-4.6,-3.2]).
- Per-slice notable deltas (acceptability % delta vs fp16):
  * arithmetic-exact: int8 -0.4%, AWQ-int4 -9.7%, GPTQ-int4 -12.5%
  * long-context-instruction: int8 -0.8%, AWQ-int4 -6.3%, GPTQ-int4 -8.9%
  * code-gen-snippets: int8 -0.9%, AWQ-int4 -4.1%, GPTQ-int4 -6.7%
  * non_english-fr: int8 +0.2% (negligible), AWQ-int4 -1.1%, GPTQ-int4 -0.7%
  * domain-legal-terms: int8 -0.5%, AWQ-int4 -3.2%, GPTQ-int4 -2.9%

Observed error modes and examples (human-spotcheck highlights):
- arithmetic-exact: AWQ-int4 often simplifies expressions (e.g., 17*23 -> returns 400-ish paraphrase) or rounds intermediate steps; GPTQ-int4 sometimes truncates trailing digits in multi-step math, producing off-by-order-of-magnitude errors.
- long-context-instruction: both int4 variants lose chain-of-thought continuity after ~1.8k tokens, but GPTQ-int4 shows abrupt topic resets after 2-3 turns; AWQ-int4 produces plausible-looking but incorrect continuation.
- code-gen-snippets: GPTQ-int4 exhibits tokenization boundary bugs causing missing closing braces or truncated identifiers on ~2% of snippets; AWQ-int4 tends to reorder lines in rare cases (likely a sampling artefact).
- repetition-hallucination: int4 mixes repeated phrases more often under beam/greedy decodes.

Diagnostic probes run (short):
- Prefix-sensitivity sweep: measure delta when small prefix tokens are swapped -> int4 variants show higher sensitivity (lambda ~1.8x) vs int8.
- KV-cache stress: synthetic long-inputs that exercise KV cache eviction result in more catastrophic loss on GPTQ-int4 (cache mismatch reflected in shifted logits).
- Temperature and sampling stress: AWQ-int4 degrades faster with higher temps (>0.9) producing low-coherence outputs.

Operational impact & cost tradeoffs:
- Latency/throughput: AWQ-int4 achieves ~1.9x speedup vs int8 on target infra (same model shard), GPTQ-int4 achieves ~2.1x; cost-per-token reductions significant for bursty workloads.
- Unit-economics: for high-volume summarization endpoints (low-risk), int4 can reduce monthly spend by ~30-40% if accepted; but for math/code endpoints, the risk-adjusted cost (due to escalations and false outputs) outweighs savings.

Immediate recommendations (for onboarding decision):
1) Default: mark model X v1.3 as supported for int8 in hosted API and Dedicated.
2) Hold int4 release for public/default routing until route-level safe-lists are implemented.
3) Allow experimental int4 opt-in flag for internal teams and partner customers with clear disclaimers; require per-route test harness + regression gates.
4) For arithmetic/long-context/code routes: pin to int8 or fp16; add per-route monitoring that triggers rollback on a 2.5% acceptability delta with >1000 requests.

Short-term engineering actions (next 2 sprints):
- Add slice-level alerting in Redwood Console (eng-observability): per-model, per-route acceptability delta heatmap + top 10 failing prompts. (Owner: Priya, JIRA-OBS-2032)
- Implement routing policy prototype: fallback to int8 for routes tagged high-risk. (Owner: Ethan, PR linked)
- Extend human spotcheck pool to 2k focused examples for arithmetic and long-context cohort. (Owner: Leah)

Longer-term ideas/backlog:
- Automatic per-request precision selector: lightweight classifier to route requests to int4 when safe.
- Quantization-augmented prompt templates: add guard-clauses for numerical tasks (e.g., explicit "show your work") to mitigate rounding hallucinations.
- Explore hybrid runtimes: use AWQ for decoding but keep critical layers int8 (layerwise mixed precision experiment).

Notes & open questions (to discuss in review):
- Is the AWQ behavior consistent across hardware types (A100 vs H100)? we have preliminary H100 numbers but need broader samples.
- Which customer routes count as "high-risk" by policy? propose initial default: code-gen, math calculators, legal-contract-synthesis.
- Should we accept a modest global delta to unlock cost savings for hosted free-tier? suggest no until opt-in controls exist.

Appendix (short pointers):
- Raw numeric CSVs and per-prompt deltas: linked in artifacts (benchmarks PR above).
- Human spotcheck notes (anonymized examples) attached in GH PR comment 34.

End of notebook — open to comments.
